dz.headline: Algeria’s parallel market asks 27 700 dinars for 100 euros
dz.dek: Currency dealers offered 27 450 dinars to buy 100 euros on Tuesday, against the central bank’s official rate of 150,49 dinars per euro.
paragraphs: Currency dealers in Algeria asked 27 700 dinars for 100 euros on the parallel market on Tuesday 24 November, while offering 27 450 dinars to buy the same amount. The selling quote equals 277 dinars per euro, according to rates reported by Algerie360.
The Bank of Algeria set the official euro rate at 150,49 dinars per euro. The two prices leave a wide gap between the parallel market and the banking circuit for people exchanging euros.
Dealers quoted 24 600 dinars to buy 100 US dollars and 24 900 dinars to sell them. For 100 pounds sterling, the buying quote was 29 500 dinars and the selling quote was 30 000 dinars.

dz.headline: Algeria targets 2028 end to fertiliser imports as phosphate mine starts
dz.dek: The government says the Bled el Hadba project will supply domestic fertiliser and support non-hydrocarbon exports after an investment of nearly 5.3 billion dollars.
paragraphs: Algeria plans to stop importing fertilisers and compound fertilisers in 2028, after the Bled el Hadba phosphate deposit in Tébessa enters production fin 2027. The presidency announced the timetable on Tuesday 24 November after a meeting chaired by President Abdelmadjid Tebboune.

The project is valued at nearly 5.3 billion dollars, equivalent to 717,749 billion dinars in the 2027 finance bill, according to the report. The presidency said domestic production would replace imports; the project’s stated goals also include food security and higher non-hydrocarbon exports.

Plans include phosphate-processing complexes at Bled el Hadba and Oued El Kebrit, in Souk Ahras province, as well as a rail line linking the deposit to Annaba port and a phosphate terminal. The project is expected to extract 10 million tonnes of phosphate and produce 6 million tonnes of fertiliser a year.

dz.headline: Algeria opens public housing sales in 21 provinces to diaspora
dz.dek: The online application is open to Algerians abroad, but applicants must deliver identity and registration documents in person within 15 days.
paragraphs: Algeria’s National Real Estate Promotion Company has opened sales of free-market promotional housing in 21 provinces to residents and Algerians living abroad. Applicants can register through the company’s online platform, which generates a registration form for printing.

After registering, candidates must submit that form, a birth certificate extract and a copy of their national identity card to the relevant project directorate in person. The company gives them 15 days from registration to file the complete documents; applications are automatically cancelled if the deadline is missed.
Virtual visits are available only for properties in Blida, Tlemcen and Boumerdès. The platform does not display prices for any of the homes on offer.

dz.headline: Tebboune names Karim Zaghib to lead Algeria's lithium-battery factory
dz.dek: The Algerian scientist, who spent 28 years at Hydro-Québec in Canada, will transfer his expertise to build battery manufacturing at home.
paragraphs: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune has appointed Karim Zaghib to lead the country's lithium-battery factory project, with a mandate to transfer his expertise and develop the industry locally. Zaghib, born in Constantine in 1963, has worked on lithium batteries for more than three decades.

His record includes more than 450 scientific publications and participation in more than 970 patents. At Hydro-Québec, the Canadian company, he spent 28 years helping develop rechargeable batteries that were commercialised, according to Echorouk Online.

His work included lithium iron phosphate batteries, now a major option for electric vehicles and electricity storage. The report gives no construction schedule or production target for the Algerian factory.

dz.headline: Algeria takes 133 cruise passengers to five sites near Algiers
dz.dek: Le Champlain called at Algiers after Annaba, with a tour spanning the capital's landmarks and Tipasa's UNESCO-listed archaeological site.
paragraphs: Le Champlain, a cruise ship carrying 133 tourists of different nationalities, called at the port of Algiers 48 hours after docking in Annaba. The Algiers stop includes a tour of five sites in the capital and Tipasa, a coastal city.

The itinerary covers Algiers' Great Mosque, whose minaret is 265 metres tall, the Martyrs' Memorial, the Bardo National Museum and the neo-Moorish Grande Poste. Visitors are also due at Tipasa's archaeological site, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site. Algeria's National Tourism Office welcomed the ship and gave foreign tourists promotional materials about the country.
The stop was organised by Liledo Travel, a tourism agency. Algeria has set a target of attracting 8 million foreign tourists by 2029.

ao.headline: Angola's MPLA prepares December congress as Carneiro awaits court ruling
ao.dek: The former leadership hopeful was excluded over alleged false signatures and has asked the Constitutional Court to stop the meeting.
paragraphs: Angola's ruling Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) is due to hold its congress on 9 and 10 December, with President João Lourenço the sole candidate to lead the party. General Higino Carneiro, whose bid was rejected, is waiting for a Constitutional Court decision on his request to halt the meeting.

Carneiro's team said he still hopes the court will stop the congress in its current form. The MPLA rejected his candidacy over alleged forged signatures after internal appeals, and a court previously declined his first request to suspend the process because party appeal deadlines were still running.

The party has opened a disciplinary case against Carneiro, a member for more than 50 years, and sent the alleged-signature matter to prosecutors. Its internal campaign runs from 15 November to 3 December; Carneiro's team said he was still considering whether to attend if the court had not ruled by 9 December.

ao.headline: Angola’s central bank reports women hold 41.3% of mid-level management posts
ao.dek: At a gender-equality workshop in Luanda, a separate assessment found women’s share of leadership positions fell to 9% in larger organisations.
paragraphs: Angola’s central bank reported that women held 41.3% of its mid-level management posts at a gender-equality workshop in Luanda on Monday, 23 November. The central bank and the United Nations Global Compact in Angola organised the meeting to discuss women’s participation in financial-sector decision-making.

Eliana Pereira dos Santos, the Global Compact’s executive director in Angola, presented an assessment of organisations in its local network. It found women’s representation in leadership fell from about 51% in smaller organisations to 9% in larger ones. She called for institutional policies with targets, indicators and transparent career-progression criteria.

PwC Angola presented a diagnosis of gender equality in the financial sector, while Banco de Fomento Angola shared practices. The meeting ended with a discussion involving regulators and financial-institution representatives.

ao.headline: BAI joins Luanda Semba Sound Festival on 28 November
ao.dek: The Angolan bank is linking the event to its 30 years of activity and says it will support the promotion and preservation of cultural heritage.
paragraphs: Banco Angolano de Investimentos (BAI), an Angolan bank, will join the Semba Sound Festival at Luanda Bay on 28 November, as part of events marking its 30 years of activity.

The festival celebrates Angolan music and cultural identity. BAI said its participation supports projects to promote and preserve national cultural heritage, and aims to help document semba and pass it on to younger generations. The programme includes musicians Paulo Flores, Yuri da Cunha, Ary, C4 Pedro and Eddy Tussa.
BAI said the event will also bring the bank closer to its clients, staff and communities.

bj.headline: Benin police report 1 415 arrests in security operations
bj.dek: The campaign, launched on 12 November 2026, also dismantled 177 ghettos and seized 18 firearms, police officials said in Cotonou.
paragraphs: Benin’s Republican Police arrested 1 415 people and dismantled 177 ghettos during its fifth special security operation, officials said in Cotonou on Tuesday 24 November 2026. The campaign began on 12 November and targeted crime-prone areas and networks involved in possessing, using and selling psychotropic drugs.

Police also seized 18 firearms in operations intended to prevent violent theft. On roads, officers recorded 19 126 speeding violations involving light and heavy vehicles, alongside 2 668 traffic-light violations and 2 066 cases of riding without a helmet. Police leaders said checks would continue on main roads.
The wider police report also recorded seizures of 8 931 kg of counterfeit pharmaceutical products, more than five tonnes of cannabis and 77 403 CFA625 linked to various trafficking activities.

bj.headline: Benin launches platform for microfinance loans of 50 000 to CFA50 million
bj.dek: The national financial-inclusion platform lets registered clients choose offers, with repayment periods from three to 36 months and terms shown before signing.
paragraphs: Benin’s National Microfinance Fund launched the National Financial Inclusion Platform on Tuesday 24 November, offering loans from 50 000 to CFA50 million through the government’s 48-hour credit programme. The loan amount depends on the applicant’s profile.

Applicants must first be registered by a participating microfinance institution, which sets the client’s borrowing ceiling. After registering at an agency, customers use their personal identification number or unique borrower ID to access the platform and select an eligible offer. Monthly instalments appear before electronic signing, which requires a code sent by SMS.

Lenders have 48 hours from contract signature to transfer funds to a bank account or electronic-money wallet. Repayment terms run from three to 36 months; interest depends on the offer, insurance fees may apply, and each contract states the withdrawal period. 14 institutions participate, including FECECAM, PADME, Finadev, Coris Meso Finance and Africa Finances; assistance is available on 7320.

bj.headline: Coris Bank Bénin opens share sale ahead of listing on West Africa's regional stock exch...
bj.dek: The bank is offering 4,1 million existing shares for CFA19,19 billion, with public subscriptions scheduled for 7 to 11 December.
paragraphs: Coris Bank International Bénin launched a public share sale in Cotonou on Tuesday 24 November, the first step toward listing on the Bourse régionale des valeurs mobilières (BRVM), the regional stock exchange of West African francophone states. The offer covers 4,1 million existing shares held by Coris Holding, for a total of CFA19,19 billion.

Public investors will pay 4 CFA700 per share; Coris Group employees have a separate offer at 3 CFA760. Buyers need a securities account through Coris Bourse or a member of the placement syndicate. The West African Monetary Union's financial markets authority approved the operation on 11 November.

At the end of 2025, the bank had total assets of CFA850,3 billion and ranked third among 14 banks in Benin. It reported net income of CFA4,5 billion for the first half of 2026, up 80% from a year earlier.

bj.headline: Benin’s Economic and Social Council urges stronger reporting of violence against women
bj.dek: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané says laws and nationwide sessions need to be matched by prevention, easier reporting and support for victims.
paragraphs: Benin’s Economic and Social Council is urging stronger prevention, reporting and protection for victims of violence against women and girls. Its president, Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, made the call on Wednesday, 25 November, as the country marked the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women and opened 16 days of activism.

Bio Tchané cited two laws, enacted in 2012 and 2021, and the creation of the National Institute of Women. The council has held sessions on the 2021 law in every department, with the health and social affairs and microfinance ministries, to explain people’s rights and duties and inform victims about protection available to them.

He said responsibility also rests with local authorities, families, religious and traditional leaders, civil society and citizens. The council wants more awareness, easier ways to report abuse, stronger listening and support for victims, and education in respect and equality from an early age.

bj.headline: Benin’s media ministry seeks 24.38% budget increase for 2027
bj.dek: The proposed CFA12,39 billion allocation includes funding for audiovisual production, professional training and wider broadcast coverage.
paragraphs: Benin’s Communication Ministry has asked for a 24.38% increase in its 2027 budget, seeking 12 390 094 CFA890 compared with 9 961 132 CFA921 in 2026. Communication Minister Aurélie Adam Soulé Zoumarou presented the request to the National Assembly’s budget committee on Tuesday, 24 November.

The proposed increase is 2 428 961 CFA969, with more than three-quarters of the rise attributed to purchases of goods and services, according to details reported by L’Événement Précis. The ministry allocated 11 225 937 CFA037 to its “Communication and media” programme and 1 164 157 CFA853 to management and support.

The plan includes improving broadcasts in remote areas, expanding programmes in national languages, supporting Beninese audiovisual production and training media professionals. Parliament has yet to vote on the proposed budget.

bw.headline: Botswana Power Corporation seeks 33% tariff rise for April 2027
bw.dek: The proposal would lift average commercial rates from P2.11 to P2.76 per kilowatt-hour, with no government subsidy to cushion customers.
paragraphs: Botswana Power Corporation has asked regulators to approve a 33% weighted average electricity tariff increase, to take effect in April 2027. Average commercial tariffs would rise from P2.11 to P2.76 per kilowatt-hour, a jump of about 31%.

The Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority is still considering the application, which includes no government subsidy for consumers. Mmantlha Sankoloba, chief executive of the Botswana Exporters and Manufacturers Association, warned that higher power and fuel costs could push companies and potential foreign investors toward regional rivals that subsidise operating costs.
An average nine percent electricity tariff increase took effect in August 2026. In October, diesel rose by P2.83 a litre and petrol by P1.54 a litre.

bw.headline: Botswana seeks P4.7 billion from investors in debt auction on November 27
bw.dek: The sale is a test of how much domestic appetite remains for the government's debt, with three-quarters of the money maturing within six months.
paragraphs: The Bank of Botswana will go to the market on November 27 seeking P4.7 billion, offering five government securities under the state's P85 billion Government Note Programme. The central bank announced the auction on November 16, and the government borrows from domestic investors under the programme rather than from foreign lenders.

Treasury bills make up P3.4 billion of the offering, split evenly between a three-month bill maturing on March 3, 2027 and a six-month bill maturing on June 2, 2027. Bidding closes at 10:00 on November 27, with results at noon and settlement on December 2.

bw.headline: Botswana's non-diamond sector grew 1.6% as headline growth hit 8.7%
bw.dek: Diamond production lifted the quarterly figure, while borrowing costs and inflation are squeezing businesses and household budgets.
paragraphs: Botswana's economy grew 8.7% in the most recent quarter, but the non-diamond private sector expanded by just 1.6%, according to figures discussed at a Bank Gaborone roundtable in the capital. The non-diamond sector accounts for almost two-thirds of the economy.

Economist and former Bank of Botswana deputy governor Keith Jefferis said fluctuations in diamond production had strongly influenced headline growth, making it a poor guide to conditions for businesses and households. Private-sector credit declined about 3% over 12 months as high borrowing costs constrained expansion, while projected year-end inflation was approaching 10%.

Government borrowing rates were easing, offering modest, indirect relief on the price of credit. Bank Gaborone managing director Tsaone Raboloko told attendees that resilience needed to give way to transformation.

bw.headline: Botswana's road toll reaches 189 deaths, with tire failures uncounted
bw.dek: Crashes killed 189 people and seriously injured 448 between January and September 2026, including 165 fatal crashes, according to the assistant transport minister.
paragraphs: Botswana recorded 189 road deaths and 448 serious injuries in crashes from January to September 2026, including 165 fatal crashes, according to figures cited by assistant minister of transport and infrastructure Letlhogonolo Barongwang. He named speeding, drunk driving, distraction and failure to obey traffic rules as major contributors.

The published figures gave no separate count of crashes involving tire failure, and no estimate of how many involved heat. The source says heat can speed the chemical aging of tires and that hot weather adds stress to tires that are old, underinflated or overloaded.
Botswana's government reports recurring heat waves above 40 degrees Celsius. The source found no evidence that rising temperatures are causing more tire-related deaths in the country.

bw.headline: Botswana's diamond naming campaign faces US regulatory hurdle
bw.dek: Lab-grown diamond producers are invoking the US Federal Trade Commission's existing guidance as Botswana seeks to distinguish mined stones from laboratory-made alternatives.
paragraphs: Botswana's effort to reserve the word "diamond" for natural stones faces a hurdle in the United States, where the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), the consumer regulator that oversees jewellery advertising, is scheduled to review its Jewelry Guides in 2028. The report describes the US as the world's largest diamond consumer market.

The Diamond Producers Council, which represents lab-grown diamond manufacturers, told JCK Online, an international jewellery publication, that President Duma Boko's position conflicts with US consumer protection principles. The council said Botswana cannot set the terminology for diamond sales in the United States.

The dispute follows the November 10 signing of the Paris Declaration on Natural Diamonds between Botswana and France. The FTC's 2018 revision removed "synthetic" from its recommended descriptions for laboratory-manufactured diamonds.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso’s biodiversity platform reviews 2025 recommendations
bf.dek: The national science-policy group is also assessing biodiversity methods and preparing advice for decision-makers at a session in Ouagadougou.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso’s Permanent Secretariat for Coordination of Agricultural Sector Policies and Sustainable Development opened the second plenary session of the National Science and Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services in Ouagadougou on Tuesday, 24 November 2026. The session is reviewing recommendations from its first meeting in 2025 and preparing advice for decision-makers.

The platform’s members are also receiving training on methods used to assess work by the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services. Pamoussa Ouédraogo, representing the deputy secretary of the agriculture minister, said biodiversity faces pressure from soil degradation, deforestation, climate change, pollution and habitat loss.

Ouédraogo said a recent report found biodiversity under threat, while state and partner actions seek to keep it at an acceptable level. The session is funded by the project to strengthen experts’ capacity on biodiversity and ecosystem services.

bf.headline: Three Burkina Faso communes involve residents in budget oversight
bf.dek: Citizen committees track local investments as simplified budgets help residents follow planned revenue and spending.
paragraphs: Residents in Korsimoro, Ziniaré and Nagréongo, in Burkina Faso’s Oubri region, now help shape municipal budgets and monitor public investments, with support from the Centre for Applied Studies and Research in Public Finance (CERA-FP). The budgets in the three communes rose from 2022 to 2026, Lefaso.net reported.

Residents can submit concerns during budget preparation, while local citizen dialogue and monitoring committees follow investments in health, education, water and sanitation. CERA-FP helps the three special delegations prepare simplified budgets detailing expected revenue and planned investments. Korsimoro’s first vice-president, Naba Sanem, said on 16 November that the support had helped investments for residents move forward.
About 10 media outlets visited the communes from 15 to 19 November. The work is part of a project supported by Denmark’s foreign ministry and Oxfam in Burkina Faso.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso installs first Sourou governor in Tougan
bf.dek: Kouilga Albert Zongo is tasked with coordinating government action, security work and the resettlement of displaced people when conditions permit.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso installed Kouilga Albert Zongo as the first governor of the Sourou region at a ceremony in Tougan on Tuesday, 24 November. The government created the region as part of an administrative reorganisation adopted on 2 July 2025.

Health Minister Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou presided and handed Zongo his appointment certificate and mission letter. Zongo is responsible for coordinating government action and representing residents’ aspirations. His duties include supporting security, mediating community disputes and leading the return of internally displaced people when conditions allow.
The government also expects him to support productive activities and oversee state projects. Zongo said he would bring residents together around the region’s development.

bf.headline: China pledges to continue medical mission in Burkina Faso
bf.dek: At a Ouagadougou anniversary, the Chinese ambassador announced a second team for the country’s economic capital after 17 missions.
paragraphs: China said it would continue its medical mission in Burkina Faso at an anniversary event in Ouagadougou on Tuesday, 24 November 2026. The programme began in 1976, and 17 missions have brought more than 200 Chinese doctors to the country.

Chinese ambassador Zhao Deyong said the teams had provided care and training, and worked on disease prevention. He cited the operation of the Pala University Hospital in Bobo-Dioulasso in 2025 and said China had built the regional hospital in Koudougou. Since March 2021, the medical assistance has focused more on cardiac surgery, following a request from Burkina Faso to strengthen specialties and train teams.
Zhao announced that a second mission would work in the country’s economic capital. Burkina Faso’s health minister, Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, welcomed the cooperation.

bi.headline: Burundi’s refugee agency orders urban return ahead of surprise camp checks
bi.dek: ONPRA representatives demanded formal identification from hundreds of city-dwelling refugees, threatening loss of status for those absent during verification.
paragraphs: The National Office for the Protection of Refugees and Stateless Persons (ONPRA) is launching a physical verification operation in all Burundian camps starting this week. The agency has warned that refugees living outside designated camps, particularly in urban centers, risk sanctions including the deactivation of their refugee status if they are absent during the count.

Following a tour by coordinator Richard Uwimana, refugee representatives from five camps—Musasa, Kinama, Kavumu, Nyankanda and Bwagiriza—met with ONPRA to protect students, workers and the sick living in cities. The agency responded by requiring formal documentation to justify their presence; without it, they must return to their registration sites.

Moïse, a street vendor in Bujumbura, said he cannot meet demands for business registers, tax IDs and bank accounts while operating on limited capital. He noted that such requirements are impossible for many informal traders who rely on mobile sales to support families.

bi.headline: Burundi residents demand independent inquiry into police chief's river death
bi.dek: Police in Bugendana say Sébastien Niragira killed himself, but residents of Jenda hill dispute that account and are seeking an independent investigation.
paragraphs: Sébastien Niragira, the chief of a police post in Buraza, was found dead in the Ruvyironza River on Sunday, 22 November, at the foot of Jenda hill in Bugendana commune, Gitega province, in central Burundi. Police in Bugendana say he jumped into the river, linking the act to family conflicts over an adultery case.

Residents of Jenda hill reject that explanation. They say he may have been killed elsewhere and his body thrown into the river to make it look like suicide, and they want an independent inquiry to establish the circumstances and bring any responsible people to justice. Stany Nahimana, an elected local official on the hill, said the circumstances of the death had not yet been clearly established. Police have taken the body to the regional hospital mortuary, and investigations are continuing.
SOS Médias Burundi counts more than 100 bodies and people killed in varied circumstances across Gitega province since the start of 2026.

bi.headline: Peace torch visit shuts Bubanza market for most of a day
bi.dek: Traders reopened at 16 h 30, while schools in the town’s commercial centre closed so pupils and teachers could attend the reception.
paragraphs: Burundi’s peace torch caravan disrupted trade and schooling in Bubanza on 19 November, when the market remained closed for almost the whole day and most schools in the commercial centre stopped classes. The caravan passed through the commune in western Burundi as residents gathered for its reception.

The central market reopened at 16 h 30, only an hour and a half before its usual closing time, SOS Medias Burundi reported. Traders said repeated disruptions cost them a day’s work, with incomes dependent on daily sales. Most schools shut their doors from 10 o’clock so pupils and teachers could join the welcome; pupils were told to wear civilian clothes instead of uniforms.

The 2026 caravan, its twentieth edition, began on 13 November in Bujumbura and is scheduled to end on 10 December in Gitega. Organisers say it will visit communes for community development work and provide material support to some local projects.

cm.headline: Apple revises Cameroon developer payouts under 3% digital tax
cm.dek: The U.S. technology company says the change applies to certain app sales and in-app purchases made in Cameroon.
paragraphs: Apple has changed what it pays developers on some app sales and in-app purchases in Cameroon, pointing to the country's new 3% tax on foreign digital businesses. A notice on its developer portal, dated November 17, 2026, announced the adjustment.

The levy was introduced under Cameroon's 2026 Finance Law and lets tax authorities collect from foreign digital firms with no physical base in the country. Under Article 5 ter of the General Tax Code, nonresident companies are covered once they bill Cameroonian customers more than CFA50 million in gross fees, or serve more than 1,000 users, customers or account holders there. Article 17 quater sets the rate at 3% of gross revenue earned in Cameroon.
The tax falls under the corporate income tax regime. In its circular on implementing the 2026 budget, the Ministry of Finance said the obligations rest with nonresident digital businesses.

cm.headline: Cameroon closes candidate filings for February 2027 elections
cm.dek: Elections Cameroon received at least 200 files from 27 parties in Yaoundé, while parties submitted candidacies across the country.
paragraphs: Elections Cameroon closed submissions for the February 2027 legislative and municipal elections at 23:59 on 24 November 2026. Its Yaoundé headquarters received at least 200 candidacy files from 27 political parties, and territorial offices took submissions across the country.

The governing Cameroon People's Democratic Movement submitted more than 100 files for legislative elections. The Cameroon Renaissance Movement filed seven legislative candidacies in Mfoundi, represented by its former president, Maurice Kamto. In the Littoral region, the governing party submitted more than 30 files in Wouri, while opposition lawmaker Jean-Michel Nintcheu led the list for Wouri-East.

Electoral offices must centralise and send the files to the national directorate within five days of the close. The Electoral Council is due to begin examining each candidacy on 29 November and publish accepted and rejected lists on 09 December 2026, opening the pre-election dispute process.

cm.headline: Nachtigal takes 80.8% of climate funding in Cameroon review
cm.dek: Three financing operations for the 420 MW plant totalled $48.2 million, within a government sample of 80 operations.
paragraphs: Nachtigal hydroelectric project financing accounted for 80.8% of climate funding received in a sample of operations reviewed by Cameroon’s government. Three operations associated with the plant totalled $48.2 million, or about CFA28.6 billion, out of $59.7 million in reported receipts.

The figures are in Cameroon’s First Biennial Transparency Report and Fourth National Communication on Climate Change, submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change on November 13. The review covered 80 financing operations involving 11 funding providers. The report says the amounts are neither the full climate financing mobilised in Cameroon nor the project’s total cost.

The United Kingdom provided $18.5 million in 2020 and $17.7 million in 2021, both classified as other official flows excluding export credits. France provided about $12.1 million in 2020 as an official development assistance loan.

cm.headline: Yaoundé programme trains nine content creators to earn income from their work
cm.dek: The course, run by the association O'Botama with partner Fanaka&Co, covered filming, editing, pricing, client outreach and contracts over three days.
paragraphs: Nine young content creators completed training in audiovisual production and entrepreneurship in Yaoundé from 16 to 21 November, under a 2026 programme called CREAC'T. The association O'Botama and its partner Fanaka&Co ran the course to help participants structure their activities and earn income from them.

Over three training days, participants covered framing, scriptwriting, video editing, positioning, value proposition and business models. Each trainee had to produce an original piece of content, with freedom to choose themes such as fashion, gastronomy or crafts.

Manuelle Ngono, who won first prize, said she had been creating content for a year but had learned alone until now. Fellow winner Ndoumou Atangana Arsel Fabrice said he plans to link his channel to a communications agency and is seeking financial backing and follow-up from partners.

cf.headline: Central African Republic's parliament adopts five-year military programming law
cf.dek: The 2026-2030 programme aims to professionalise the national army so it can protect the population, and needs a budget of CFA662 billion over five years.
paragraphs: The National Assembly of the Central African Republic adopted a military programming law on 23 November covering 2026 to 2030.

The programme aims to professionalise the national army so it can protect the population more effectively, according to Radio Ndeke Luka. Its implementation will require mobilising a budget of CFA662 billion over five years. Destin De Bonheur Wilikon gave further details.
The law sets out the five-year framework for the army's development, with the budget to be raised across the full period from 2026 to 2030.

cf.headline: Journalists’ union calls Central African Republic media blackout over threats
cf.dek: The union says recent pressure has particularly targeted Radio Ndeke Luka over reports on rising living costs, fuel shortages and living conditions.
paragraphs: The Union of Journalists of the Central African Republic has called on the country’s media to observe a day without information on Wednesday, 25 November, to protest threats against journalists. The union says the pressure has particularly affected Radio Ndeke Luka.

The station has been targeted for a week by people close to the government who dispute its reporting on the cost of living, fuel shortages and people’s living conditions, the union said. The union’s president, Michael Mounzatela, announced the action in an interview with Radio Ndeke Luka.

The union described the blackout as its first protest action and said further measures would follow. Radio France Internationale reported that journalists were also calling on the authorities to protect media workers and press freedom.

cf.headline: Sam-Ouandja hospital imposes daily charges on inpatients
cf.dek: A Central African Republic report also records allegations that an elderly woman died after being left without sufficient care in her bed.
paragraphs: Sam-Ouandja’s hospital in Haute-Kotto, Central African Republic, is charging patients a daily fee to stay in its inpatient ward, according to an investigation by Corbeau News Centrafrique. The hospital’s new building was funded by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

The outlet said it gathered serious testimony about the charges and care at the hospital. Its investigation reported that an elderly woman died after being left in her bed without sufficient assistance. The report did not provide the fee amount or say how many patients are affected.

Sam-Ouandja is a small locality where much of the population depends on farming, and the report says access to care is already difficult for many families. The UNDP-funded building was intended to improve hospital accommodation and inpatient conditions.

cf.headline: Witness tells court Papy Bozizé arrested six customs officers
cf.dek: At the Special Criminal Court in Bangui, the witness said the officers were detained in Bouar in 2012 while working as customs officers.
paragraphs: A protected witness told the Special Criminal Court in Bangui on 23 November that Papy Bozizé arrested six customs officers in Bouar in 2012. The witness, identified as BOS-06, said the officers were detained while carrying out their duties and that he did not know why he had been arrested.

The witness said Papy Bozizé, then commander of Military Region No. 3, had taken over customs duties, and that the officers opposed him during an operation. He said the six were taken to Bossembélé prison. Defence lawyers argued that their release on judicial instructions showed their clients were not responsible for the detention; prosecutors said judicial authorities had no control over the prison at the time.

The witness also said magistrate Éric Tambo visited regularly and brought the document ordering their release. The case concerns charges of murder, torture, cruel and degrading treatment, and enforced disappearances as crimes against humanity; further witnesses are due to testify.

cf.headline: Parity observatory finds institutions below 35% women’s representation
cf.dek: Data collected across ministries, private structures and political parties is being validated for a report on the 2016 law.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic’s National Observatory for Parity is validating data on women’s representation in public institutions, private organisations, political parties and ministries. The workshop took place on Monday, 23 November, ahead of the 10th anniversary of the parity law adopted on 24 November 2016.

Rita Adeline Feikere, the observatory’s coordinator, said initial figures show the organisations remain below the law’s 35% threshold. The law covers public, parapublic and private employment, while its stated target is 50% representation of women. The observatory says the data must be checked before it publishes a general report on the law’s first decade.
Feikere said the observatory has had no available data since it was established in 2025, preventing a precise comparison with the starting position or changes over time.

km.headline: Sambi rejects UAE evacuation terms as Comoros talks continue
km.dek: The jailed former president seeks guarantees on treatment and his return, while officials left Moroni without an agreement after a November visit.
paragraphs: Ahmed Abdallah Sambi, Comoros’ former president, has refused the terms of a proposed medical evacuation to the United Arab Emirates after a delegation visited Moroni from 19 to 22 November. Sambi has been imprisoned since 2018.

The UAE envoys offered to cover two to three years of care, with Sambi living with his family, but his passport would be taken and visits, political activity and trips to an embassy barred. A June medical report said he has cardiac ischaemia requiring an angiogram, an examination unavailable in the Comoros archipelago. Sambi wants his initial tests in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, and permission to visit his children abroad. President Azali Assoumani reportedly rejected the Tanzanian stop.
The envoys returned to Vwadjuu on Sunday to convey Assoumani’s position, then left Moroni without an agreement. Discussions could resume over the terms of Sambi’s departure.

km.headline: Comoros to inaugurate renovated Moroni high school on 25 November
km.dek: The France-funded €2.4 million renovation covers classrooms, science labs, a library, toilets and sports facilities at the school.
paragraphs: Comoros is due to inaugurate the renovated Saïd Mohamed Cheikh high school in Moroni on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, after rehabilitation work funded by France through the French Development Agency (AFD). The project’s initial budget was €2.4 million, equivalent to nearly 1.18 billion Comorian francs.

The Education Ministry and the French embassy are organising the ceremony. Work covered classrooms, science laboratories, the library, sanitation facilities and sports infrastructure, under the Bundo la Malezi programme to improve teaching conditions in Comoros.
The ceremony also marks the school’s 60th anniversary. The report says it has educated generations of students, including many of the country’s senior officials.

cg.headline: Congo employers submit 48-page tax proposals to parliament
cg.dek: UniCongo urges lawmakers to tax company income rather than turnover as they examine the 2027 finance bill.
paragraphs: The Union patronale et interprofessionnelle du Congo (UniCongo), an employers' organisation, submitted 48 pages of proposals to the National Assembly's finance commission on 23 November, during its review of the 2027 finance bill. The proposals address business conditions and tax rules affecting companies.

UniCongo president Dieudonné Ndinga Moukala led a delegation of about a dozen members. He said the document draws on businesses' experience and explains the organisation's proposals. They cover penalties, registration duties, value-added tax and the single tax on salaries, and favour taxing income over turnover, which UniCongo says better reflects companies' circumstances.
The commission, chaired by Maurice Mavoungou, is to examine the proposals and assess their scope. UniCongo hopes its concerns will be reflected in the final bill.

paragraphs: The Congo under-23 national team will play Guinea in a two-legged tie scheduled for March 22 and 30 to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. The first match takes place in Congo, with the return fixture held in Conakry.

Journal de Brazza reports that Congo advanced by beating Angola, drawing 1-1 away and winning 1-0 at home. Guinea reached this stage after defeating Botswana 7-0 at the Stade du 28-Septembre in Conakry, following a 1-0 away win.

ci.dek: The presidents made the commitment in Abidjan, where Ouattara urged German investors to consider projects under Ivory Coast's 2026-2030 development plan.
paragraphs: Ivory Coast's President Alassane Ouattara and German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier agreed to promote trade between their countries during talks in Abidjan on Monday 23 November 2026. Annual trade averaged CFA918.3 billion over the last three years, Ouattara said.

ci.headline: Europe's development bank opens Abidjan office and pledges 250 million euros
ci.dek: The bank says the new commitments will add to more than 200 million euros it has already invested in Ivory Coast, where it began operating in 2025.
paragraphs: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), a multilateral lender owned by European and other governments, opened a resident office in Abidjan on Monday 23 November and announced 250 million euros in new commitments for Ivory Coast. Its president, Odile Renaud-Basso, made the announcement during a visit that runs through 25 November.

The bank said it has already invested more than 200 million euros in the country and aims to have more than 500 million euros outstanding by the end of 2026. Earlier financing went to cashew processing, mining services, local banks and the energy transition. Ivory Coast joined the bank in December 2024 and became a country of operations in 2025.

Renaud-Basso and Digital Transition Minister Djibril Ouattara signed an agreement on technical assistance, technology-project financing and support for start-ups, but no amount was announced. A financial and technical support programme for Ivorian small and medium-sized businesses is also due to launch during her visit.

ci.headline: Credaf Group names Massetou Traoré chief executive
ci.dek: The Abidjan-based financial holding company says she will lead its seven Alios Finance subsidiaries operating in seven African countries.
paragraphs: Credaf Group, an Abidjan-based pan-African financial holding company, has appointed Massetou Traoré as chief executive. Her remit covers the group’s activities, including seven Alios Finance subsidiaries operating in seven African countries, according to a note sent to Agence Ivoirienne de Presse.

Traoré has more than 18 years of financial-sector experience, including senior roles at Citibank and Ecobank covering West and Central Africa. She most recently served as deputy chief executive of NSIA Banque Côte d’Ivoire, where she worked on strategy, business development and governance. Credaf Group chairman Serge-Aimé Bilé said her regional experience would help the subsidiaries cooperate and develop financing solutions for businesses.
The group’s transformation began after it integrated the Alios Finance entities in April 2025. The subsidiaries are based in Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Gabon, Mali, Senegal and Tunisia.

ci.headline: Endeavour Mining backs Gontougo development plan as mine construction starts
ci.dek: Vision Tanda links the Assafo-Dibibango gold project to local jobs, businesses, living conditions, education and training.
paragraphs: Endeavour Mining has launched Vision Tanda, a programme for economic and social development in Gontougo, where it is building the Assafo-Dibibango gold project. Construction began in November 2026, with investment of more than CFA700 billion, according to a company note reported by Agence Ivoirienne de Presse.

The programme covers local entrepreneurship and jobs, living conditions, education and training. Since June 2026, 277 people have received training in Tanda department, six local small and medium-sized businesses have joined mine construction, and 60 caterers are receiving support, the company said. Ivorian group Kaydan is building new villages at Iguéla and Toundiani; the first show homes at Iguéla were delivered in October 2026.

The mine, about 280 km north-east of Abidjan, is expected to produce an average of 320 000 ounces of gold a year during its first eight years. Its first gold pour is expected in the first half of 2029, with an initial operating life estimated at at least 16 years.

eg.headline: Egypt phone prices rise about 60% as buyers turn to used devices
eg.dek: The increases have hit budget models as well as high-end phones, and retailers say repeated hikes are slowing sales.
paragraphs: Mobile phone prices in Egypt have risen about 60% over the recent period, hitting all price categories and making purchases harder for consumers. Retailers on Cairo’s Abdel-Aziz Street reported slower sales as increases continued.

Abdel-Nasser Gad, a phone retailer, said prices had risen repeatedly for more than a year, burdening buyers seeking entry-level devices. Another retailer, Hafez, said some customers were switching to used phones or low-cost Chinese-made models. Mohamed Talaat, head of the mobile phones division at the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce, said the increases began before this year and have become more frequent.

Talaat said phone components, especially RAM and storage memory, make up about 20% of production costs and can rise in price every two weeks. A Monday meeting attended by the prime minister and representatives of the customs authority and telecom regulator discussed local phone manufacturing.

eg.headline: EU tightens pesticide limits for Egyptian produce from January 2027
eg.dek: The rules follow 91 EU notifications on Egyptian shipments from January to August, 81% of them involving pesticide residues.
paragraphs: Egyptian fresh-produce exporters face stricter European Union rules on pesticide residues, packaging and supply-chain compliance from January 2027 through 2030. The first change takes effect on 29 January 2027, when limits for benomyl, carbendazim and thiophanate-methyl fall to the lowest detectable level.

The EU-funded Agrinfo programme, run by Colead, reported 91 notifications on Egyptian shipments between January and August; 81% concerned pesticide residues. September brought nine more alerts, eight involving fresh produce. A spice manufacturer and exporter told an Egypt-EU agrifood dialogue in Cairo that replacing carbendazim requires field trials to test substitutes’ effects on crop protection, yields and quality.

From 5 May, difenoconazole limits will fall on many crops. Stickers on fruit and vegetables must be industrially compostable from 12 February 2028, and the EU will ban single-use plastic packaging for fresh produce under 1.5 kg from 1 January 2030, subject to member state exemptions.

eg.headline: Iraq and Egypt agree to abolish entry visas
eg.dek: The leaders announced the deal in Cairo, but gave no start date or details on which travelers will qualify.
paragraphs: Iraq and Egypt agreed to abolish entry visas between the two countries, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi said on Monday, 23 November, during his first official visit to Egypt. He announced the decision alongside Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi in Cairo.

Al-Zaidi said officials had not set a date for the change or decided which travelers it would cover, leaving both governments to work out the rules. The move would change entry requirements for people traveling between the neighboring countries, but the announcement gave no implementation timetable.

Trade between Egypt and Iraq reached USD 1.1 billion in 2024, according to Egypt’s Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics. Egyptian exports to Iraq were about USD 880 million in 2025; an Iraqi trade official also said Baghdad was weighing a supply of 10 million barrels of crude, with no price or delivery schedule set.

eg.headline: Egypt hosts building materials summit as exporters seek overseas buyers
eg.dek: The Convergence 2026 summit will bring about 100 industry, trade and investment leaders from 40 countries to Sharm El-Sheikh for a one-day gathering.
paragraphs: Egypt will host the first Global Building Materials Summit, known as CONVERGE 2026, in Sharm El-Sheikh on 29 November, with around 100 industry, trade and investment leaders expected from 40 countries. Building materials are Egypt's largest non-oil export, but manufacturers have faced higher shipping costs and softer demand after a boom last year.

Ahmed Othman, a board member of the Chamber of Building Materials Industries who heads its insulation division and chairs the summit, said organizers want Egyptian manufacturers to find buyers, investors and partners abroad. He said the gathering would focus on building long-term partnerships among manufacturers, investors, distributors and policymakers, rather than routine networking.

The one-day agenda includes sustainability, advanced manufacturing, access to global markets and industrial franchising, which lets companies enter new markets while passing on technical know-how. Othman said the choice of Sharm El-Sheikh, often called the City of Peace, was meant to show that Egypt remains a safe place to do business.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea council approves youth employment plan for 2027-2031
gq.dek: The government also greenlit new bodies for economic zones, trade facilitation, and energy security during the meeting.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea’s Interministerial Council has approved a National Plan for Employment Promotion, Self-Employment, and Youth Entrepreneurship. The plan, presented by the Ministry of Labor and Occupational Training, establishes a framework to integrate young people into the labor market and support business initiatives from 2027 to 2031.

Prime Minister Manuel Osa Nsue Nsua chaired the sixth council meeting of 2026 on Monday, November 23. During the session, officials reviewed non-oil revenue status to strengthen internal resource generation. The council also approved decrees creating the National Commission for Coordination of Development Agendas (CONAD) and the Special Economic Zones Authority (ANZEE).

Additional measures included the creation of a Single Window for Foreign Trade (VUCE) and a public company to manage state hotel assets. Energy security was addressed through new rules for minimum petroleum stocks and a draft law regulating electricity. Digital infrastructure sharing and a Maritime Single Window were also endorsed.

paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea’s Vice-President Nguema Obiang Mangue delivered a message from President Obiang Nguema Mbasogo to Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi during an official visit to Egypt. Officials examined expanding specialist training, technical assistance and information exchanges in defence and security. They also discussed potential housing, road, public-building, water-supply and sanitation projects for Ciudad de La Paz, including financing and technology transfer.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea’s national university suspends professor and expels student
gq.dek: The measures followed a recorded confrontation in which the student broke a pair of glasses and the professor slapped the student.
paragraphs: The National University of Equatorial Guinea (UNGE) suspended a professor from all teaching activity and expelled a student after a confrontation at its Papa León XIV Campus in Basupú. The university announced the measures on Tuesday, 24 November, applying the rules that govern the institution.

In a recording, the professor asks the student to hand over a pair of glasses; the student breaks them in front of the professor, who then slaps the student. The university rector’s office said the decisions form part of a zero-tolerance policy on indiscipline and violence on campus.
The rector’s office said the university should serve as a place for education, culture and values in support of national development.

er.headline: Ethiopian offensive in Tigray pushes fighting toward Eritrea
er.dek: Clashes have spread across several areas, with reported heavy artillery fire near Badme and analysts warning of a wider conflict.
paragraphs: Ethiopia's army has resumed its offensive in Tigray, pushing local armed formations toward the border with Eritrea after several weeks of relative calm. Clashes are under way in several areas, according to the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project (ACLED), a monitoring organisation.

Near Badme, a town that was a main flashpoint of the 1998-2000 Ethiopia-Eritrea war, heavy artillery fire has reportedly been used. Abdurahman Said, director of the Center for Regional Integration of the Horn of Africa, said troop concentrations along the frontier point to the danger of a large-scale conflict. Analysts cited by Deutsche Welle warned that the fighting could escalate into a regional war.

Ethiopia's stated desire for Red Sea access is another source of tension; Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has not ruled out force to take control of Eritrea's port of Assab. Relations between Ethiopia and Sudan are also worsening, though International Crisis Group analyst Magnus Taylor said a direct Ethiopia-Sudan clash is currently unlikely.

er.headline: Boulos reviews U.S. Eritrea policy after Cairo talks
er.dek: The U.S. Africa envoy met Eritrea’s foreign minister three months after beginning the review, amid persistent rumours of a secret sanctions deal.
paragraphs: Massad Boulos, President Donald Trump’s Africa envoy, began a review of U.S. policy toward Eritrea in April 2026. Three months later, he met Eritrea’s foreign minister in Cairo to discuss a new relationship between the two countries.

Rumours persist that the officials signed a secret agreement to lift sanctions and restore normal ties, but the report does not confirm a deal. Eritrea’s location on the Red Sea is a strategic concern for Washington because the surrounding corridor links the Suez Canal, Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb and Gulf of Aden.

The analysis argues that Eritrea’s strategic position does not make President Isaias Afwerki’s government a reliable partner, citing what it describes as a pattern of opposition to Western influence and regional arrangements.

er.headline: Eritrea's president leaves national unity call to proxies
er.dek: A newscaster read the appeal on television, while poet Awel Said called for unity in early November.
paragraphs: Eritrea Focus says President Isaias Afwerki has not addressed the nation himself as calls for unity and defence of the country circulate amid fighting on the border. A newscaster read a proclamation on television, and poet-orator Awel Said made a unity appeal in early November.

The article says mothers fear younger children will be conscripted for another war, after earlier generations served in Badme and Tigray. It says some Eritreans were sent to fight in those conflicts, and mothers were not told where their children were; the article says there is no list of the dead or answer for families.

The article also says national service involves forced labour and abuse, and that singer Senait Debessai has been imprisoned without charge or trial since 2003. It questions how citizens can answer a call to defend the country when the president speaks through others.

er.headline: Awate essay argues Eritrea needs a democratic developmental state
er.dek: Negusse Micael says leadership, capable institutions and public trust must work together to deliver national priorities and sustain government authority.
paragraphs: Eritrea needs a state that combines developmental leadership, effective institutions and societal legitimacy, Negusse Micael argues in an essay published by Awate on November 24. He calls the model a “Developmental Triangle” and says each foundation depends on the other two.

Micael argues that institutions should implement national priorities and operate under constitutional accountability, while government authority should rest on public participation, accountability and trust. He says Eritrea’s development debate often treats democracy, economic growth, sovereignty, national security and unity as separate concerns.

The essay says replacing current political leadership or pursuing constitutional and economic reforms in isolation would not be enough; Eritrea would need to reconfigure the relationship between political authority, state institutions and society.

ke.headline: Kenya plans 6.16 million fruit seedlings for farmers in 2027/28
ke.dek: The draft budget includes avocado, mango, citrus, coconut and date palm, alongside macadamia, cashew nut, tea and coffee seedlings.
paragraphs: Kenya plans to distribute 6.16 million seedlings to farmers in the 2027/28 financial year, according to its draft 2027 Budget Policy Statement. The programme covers avocado, mango, citrus, coconut, date palm, macadamia, cashew nut, tea and coffee.

The Treasury says the distribution is intended to move farmers towards higher-value crops. Date palms are designated for growers in Arid and Semi-Arid Lands, where cultivation will focus on crops suited to local conditions. The draft also proposes more processing and cold-chain infrastructure for avocados and mangoes.

The statement gives no programme cost, procurement process, county delivery schedule, crop-by-crop allocation or eligibility rules. Kenya’s avocado harvest reached 694,000 tons in 2025; the Agriculture and Food Authority projects 727,000 tons in 2026.

ke.headline: High Court summons Mombasa police chief over unexecuted KSh154.4 million debt warrant
ke.dek: Justice Jairus Ngaah ordered OCS Eliud Kimwele to explain why officers have not arrested Finance Executive Evans Oanda under a warrant received in June.
paragraphs: Kenya’s High Court has ordered Eliud Kimwele, the officer in charge of Mombasa Central Police Station, to appear on December 11 and explain why he has not executed an arrest warrant against county Finance Executive Evans Oanda. The warrant concerns an approximately KSh154.4 million debt owed to Kooba Limited under court orders.

Justice Jairus Ngaah issued the summons after Kooba director Richard Bell asked the court to make Inspector-General of Police Douglas Kanja take over enforcement. Kooba says officers received the warrant on June 30, after it was issued on June 26, but have not acted. The judge directed Kimwele to appear personally, rather than submit a report.

The debt stems from a 2022 judgment awarding Kooba KSh151 million over the county’s handling of approvals for a proposed data centre. Interest and costs have since raised the amount to approximately KSh154.4 million. The county’s lawyer asked for 14 days to respond to Kooba’s application.

ke.headline: Africa’s Green Economy Summit lists 20 projects seeking over US$500 million
ke.dek: The deal books include a Kenyan proposal to reuse electric motorcycle batteries as stationary energy storage systems.
paragraphs: Africa’s Green Economy Summit has published two investment deal books listing the first 20 confirmed projects across 13 African countries, which are seeking more than US$500 million in total. The projects include solar developments in Zimbabwe, battery reuse in Kenya and clean technology manufacturing in Nigeria.

The Infrastructure Deal Book and SMME Deal Book describe project maturity, capital sought and commercial models for investors, financiers and development partners. Kenya’s Spiro ESS proposes repurposing electric motorcycle batteries into stationary energy storage systems, extending their lifecycles and supporting more reliable electricity supply.

The books also feature MamboAnesu Energy, a phased solar project in Zimbabwe planned for 200 MW, and an Egyptian farm combining irrigation, renewable energy and digital management. The summit’s fifth edition is scheduled for 23 to 26 February 2027 in Cape Town.

ke.headline: Nairobi county launches 16-day campaign against gender-based violence
ke.dek: Activities across all 17 sub-counties will link residents with survivor support, justice, healthcare and psychosocial services.
paragraphs: Nairobi City County launched its 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign on Wednesday at Eastleigh High School, with activities planned across the capital. The campaign will bring together communities, schools and neighbourhoods with government agencies, development partners and civil society groups.

Across all 17 sub-counties, the campaign will focus on survivor-centred support and prevention, according to Dr Irene Muchoki, the county's chief officer for inclusivity. Services for survivors are being expanded to justice, healthcare and psychosocial support, with protection made available at grassroots level.

During the 16 days, the county's Gender and Inclusivity Sub-Sector will run awareness activities and community dialogues. County Executive Committee Member Rosemary Kariuki said government agencies, development partners and communities would work together on prevention and survivor protection.

za.headline: Western Cape High Court sets aside Phala Phala impeachment report
za.dek: The court ruled the panel had to find sufficient evidence to justify an inquiry, not merely information about the theft at Ramaphosa's farm.
paragraphs: The Western Cape High Court on Wednesday set aside in its entirety the independent panel report that underpinned Parliament's impeachment proceedings against President Cyril Ramaphosa. Judge President Nolwazi Penelope Mabindla-Boqwana, delivering the judgment in Cape Town, ruled the report fundamentally flawed. The case concerns the theft of approximately $580 000 (about R9.6 million) from Ramaphosa's Phala Phala game farm in Limpopo, reported on 9 February 2020.

Mabindla-Boqwana said the panel had to establish whether sufficient evidence existed to justify an impeachment inquiry, and that misreading that duty would undermine the whole report. She held that the Constitutional Court's earlier ruling concerned the constitutionality of Parliament's December 2022 vote, not the validity of the report, so it made no binding finding on the report.

Ramaphosa had obtained an interdict in late July halting public hearings by the impeachment committee until the court decided the matter. The case was heard over three days in September. The court also found his delay in bringing the review was not unreasonable, as it was linked to the Constitutional Court proceedings.

za.headline: ANC and ActionSA prepare 18-party Johannesburg coalition
za.dek: Herman Mashaba is expected to become mayor, while the ANC is set to retain the speaker and finance posts; the deputy mayor remains undecided.
paragraphs: The African National Congress (ANC) and ActionSA are finalising a coalition arrangement to share power in Johannesburg, South Africa’s economic hub. ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba is expected to become mayor when councillors elect office-bearers on Friday. The ANC is expected to retain the speaker’s position and finance portfolio.

The deputy mayor’s post remains unresolved, with the ANC, the uMkhonto Wesizwe party and the Economic Freedom Fighters discussed as possible contenders, Daily Maverick reported. The proposed framework brings 18 parties together, excluding the Democratic Alliance, Freedom Front Plus and African Christian Democratic Party. The council’s first sitting on Monday swore in councillors but postponed the office-bearer elections to give parties more time to negotiate.

The ANC won 20.25% of the vote and 64 seats in the 270-member council, while ActionSA won 16.27% and 42 seats. The Democratic Alliance took 91 seats, the most of any party, but fell short of the 136 required for a majority. The wider ANC-ActionSA agreement would give ActionSA the mayoralties in Johannesburg and Tshwane, while the ANC keeps Ekurhuleni’s mayoralty.

za.headline: South African blueberry exports stay on track despite port delays
za.dek: Growers report yields rising as older plants are replaced, while European and UK demand offsets Middle East shipment disruptions.
paragraphs: South Africa’s blueberry export season remains on course to meet its initial forecasts through week 44, despite port delays and changing weather, the International Blueberry Organization said. Production is moving from northern growing areas to the southern regions expected to supply most exports for the rest of the season.

Brent Walsh, chief executive of Berries ZA, said northern production matched expectations because there were no material frost events. Short rain in the south requires growers to time orchard work carefully, he said. Replacing older varieties with newer genetics has lifted yields per hectare and fruit quality, while planted area has stayed relatively stable.

Wind-related disruptions at South African shipping terminals have required the industry to work with container terminal operators on efficiency. Middle East instability has reduced targeted shipments there, but demand from Europe and the UK has made up the shortfall. Berries ZA is also advancing market-access processes in China and India and has taken part in visits to Japan, Vietnam and South Korea.

za.headline: South African court postpones Sibiya case to 9 February
za.dek: Investigators are seeking more time to examine four devices allegedly wiped before the former deputy police chief’s arrest and reconstruct a hotel scene.
paragraphs: A Randburg magistrate’s court postponed former deputy national police commissioner Shadrack Sibiya’s case to 9 February 2027, after the State sought more time for its investigation. Sibiya, 59, remains in custody and faces six charges, including rape, human trafficking and the sexual grooming of a minor.

State prosecutor Zwelethu Mata told the court on Tuesday, 24 November, that investigators had hired an expert to recover information from four seized digital devices and were awaiting a report. Prosecutors alleged during Sibiya’s October bail proceedings that he wiped his phones before his arrest and asked a 16-year-old complainant to delete their messages. Sibiya denies the allegations.

Investigators are also waiting for a Sandton hotel floor plan to complete a reconstruction and photographic record of the alleged scene involving an 18-year-old woman. Prosecutors are considering moving the case to the Johannesburg High Court for trial.

za.headline: NSRI warns visitors not to board Cape Town’s BOS400 wreck
za.dek: The warning followed the rescue of an injured American tourist from rocks near Maori Bay after he was caught in rough water.
paragraphs: A rescue team pulled an injured American tourist from rocks near the BOS400 shipwreck at Maori Bay, near Cape Town, on Monday, 23 November. He had fallen into the sea while reportedly trying to board the wreck and was caught in rip currents and heavy swells.

The National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI) said the man reached the wreck, then re-entered the water to retrieve his cellphone from nearby rocks. His brother and a friend got help from a passer-by, and rescue teams approached from land and sea. Medics treated him for hypothermia before taking him to the NSRI’s Hout Bay base; he was released to his companions without needing further treatment.

The NSRI warned the public against boarding the wreck, citing unstable structures, submerged metal, cold water and dangerous rip currents. The three Americans had competed in a Cape Town triathlon over the weekend.

ng.headline: Obaigbena says he received no police invitation over First Bank dispute
ng.dek: The chairman of THISDAY (Nigerian newspaper group) and ARISE (Nigerian television network) says settlement talks with First Bank and GHL are continuing after a Supreme Court.
paragraphs: Nduka Obaigbena, chairman of Nigerian media companies THISDAY, a newspaper group, and ARISE, a television network, said he had received no police invitation or other law-enforcement communication over a dispute involving First Bank and his media organisations. In a statement issued by his office in Ikoyi, Lagos, he denied reports that police had declared him wanted and denied threatening First Bank chief executive Olusegun Alebiosu.

Obaigbena's office said it had checked all his addresses and found no invitation related to an investigation. It linked the reports to a financial dispute involving First Bank, GHL, THISDAY Newspapers and ARISE Television, and said talks were under way to settle outstanding issues. The statement said the Supreme Court ruled unanimously, 5-0, for GHL in its case against First Bank on July 3, 2026.

The statement said First Bank and GHL had explored an out-of-court settlement since the ruling, while efforts to resolve debts allegedly owed to the media companies were also continuing. Obaigbena said he had spoken with senior police officials on November 19 about the proposed state police system.

ng.headline: Obi mourns Pete Edochie, 79, for bringing Nigerian culture to global audiences
ng.dek: The former Anambra governor praised the veteran actor’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart.
paragraphs: Peter Obi, a presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress and former Anambra State governor, mourned veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie after his family announced his death on Wednesday. Edochie was 79.

In a condolence message on X, Obi said Edochie helped bring Nigerian and African traditions to audiences around the world, particularly through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart. Obi also praised the actor’s command of English and Igbo and his experience in broadcasting.

President Bola Tinubu also mourned Edochie, calling him a Nollywood pioneer whose roles promoted Nigerian culture internationally, according to The Punch. Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah described the death as a personal loss to the state, Premium Times reported.

et.headline: Ethiopia’s central bank holds forex supply at $140 million as bids exceed it
et.dek: Banks bid $160.76 million on November 24, while the birr’s marginal rate rose to 159.40 per dollar from 159.18 at the previous auction.
paragraphs: The National Bank of Ethiopia kept its foreign-currency allocation at $140 million in an auction on November 24, while bids from commercial banks totalled $160.76 million. The marginal exchange rate rose to 159.40 birr per US dollar, from 159.18 in the previous auction on November 10.

The 32 banks that submitted bids were up from 31 in the prior round, and 28 secured allocations, compared with 26 previously. The weighted average rate for successful bids increased to 160.73 birr per dollar from 159.70, according to the central bank’s auction results.

Total bids were 2.57% higher than the $156.73 million submitted two weeks earlier. The November 24 auction was the fourth of six scheduled for the October–December quarter; the bank plans to offer $140 million in each round, for a quarterly total of $840 million.

et.headline: Abiy offers to host inclusive talks on Sudan war
et.dek: Ethiopia invited Sudan’s military, political and civilian groups to negotiations, and two Sudanese factions welcomed the proposal on Tuesday.
paragraphs: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has invited Sudan’s military, political and civilian groups to talks hosted by Ethiopia, proposing a dialogue to end the war. The offer was announced on Tuesday, Nov. 24, with no immediate response from Sudan’s army or the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

Somoud, a civilian coalition led by former Sudanese Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok, welcomed the initiative, as did the RSF-affiliated Transitional Peace Government. Its information minister, Khaled Ahmed Danna, said the administration was ready to engage. Abiy said the process should be Sudanese-led and include all stakeholders.

The offer comes after both countries closed each other’s consulates and expelled diplomatic staff in early November. Sudan has accused Ethiopia of allowing drone attacks launched from its territory; Ethiopia denies supporting the RSF.

et.headline: Health experts seek more climate funding for Africa’s malaria response
et.dek: The Roll Back Malaria Partnership says health gets only 6% of climate finance, despite rising pressure on health systems and medicine delivery.
paragraphs: Health experts at the International Conference on Public Health in Africa in Addis Ababa called for more investment in climate-resilient healthcare, warning that climate change is extending malaria transmission into previously unaffected areas and disrupting medicine delivery.

Dr. Michael Adekunle-Charles, chief executive of the Roll Back Malaria Partnership to End Malaria, said malaria kills about 620,000 people worldwide each year, with roughly 95% of those deaths in Africa, mostly among children under five. He said only 6% of climate financing goes to health, and urged donors, African governments and private businesses to increase funding.

Dr. Elizabeth Juma, who leads the World Health Organization’s Africa office programme for eliminating neglected tropical diseases, said climate risks should be built into national health strategies. She warned that extreme weather damages health infrastructure and disrupts essential services.

gh.headline: Ghana raises more than $240 million from 5G spectrum allocation
gh.dek: The revised licensing framework opens three frequency bands to competing operators, with consumers expected to access 5G early next year.
paragraphs: Ghana has secured more than $240 million by allocating spectrum for fifth-generation (5G) mobile services, Communications Minister Samuel Nartey George told Parliament during debate on the 2027 Budget. The allocation covers the 700 megahertz, 2.3 gigahertz and 3 gigahertz bands.

The government changed the licensing framework after the National Communications Authority removed exclusivity from the wholesale 5G infrastructure licence held by Next Gen Infraco Limited in July 2026. The authority invited applications, and MTN Ghana, Telecel Ghana and Goal Telecommunications qualified to advance in the licensing process.
George said President John Dramani Mahama was expected to announce the network’s launch before the end of 2026. Consumers are expected to begin using the service early next year.

gh.headline: GTEC freezes new PhD accreditation applications after universities admit students
gh.dek: Eduwatch backs the move to protect doctoral standards but says earlier oversight could have prevented students from starting programmes under scrutiny.
paragraphs: Ghana’s tertiary education regulator, the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC), has stopped processing fresh accreditation applications for PhD programmes. Africa Education Watch Executive Director Kofi Asare backed the freeze, saying it was needed to protect doctoral education standards, but said it came after several universities had completed admissions and some students had started their programmes.

Speaking on JoyNews on Tuesday, November 24, Asare said GTEC should guide and monitor universities before admissions, not rely only on audits and sanctions after breaches. He warned that students can face uncertainty over institutional failures they did not control. GTEC says its review will assess universities’ academic staff, research facilities, supervision capacity and other resources.
A separate report said GTEC’s PhD audit would take under a month and that the commission had ordered a business school to revoke unaccredited admissions.

gh.dek: The arrest followed a tax sweep at Kwame Nkrumah Circle that led officials to close 48 shops over non-compliance.
paragraphs: Police arrested a mobile phone dealer at Kwame Nkrumah Circle in Accra on Tuesday afternoon after he allegedly sent GH¢1,000 by mobile money to a tax official during a tax enforcement exercise. The operation also resulted in 48 shops being closed over tax non-compliance.

Joseph Annan, the Accra Area Enforcement Manager of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), told Joy Business that the trader claimed he had paid tax through an unidentified officer at the authority's Adabraka office. After questioning cast doubt on that claim, Annan ordered the shop shut; the trader then allegedly sent him the money. Customs Division officers of the GRA arrested the dealer, who is to give a statement while Annan also writes one, he said.
The GRA set up a temporary registration and payment stand for businesses under the Modified Taxation Scheme. The exercise was conducted with the Union of Mobile Phone Dealers of Ghana.

gh.headline: GMet forecasts 39°C heat in northern Ghana and southern storms
gh.dek: Bolgatanga and Nalerigu are expected to reach 39°C, while dawn mist and fog could cut visibility across coastal, forest and mountain areas.
paragraphs: Ghana's Meteorological Agency (GMet) forecasts highs of 39°C in Bolgatanga and Nalerigu on Wednesday, with dry, hazy conditions in the north. Tamale, Wa and Jirapa are forecast to reach 38°C.

In the south, GMet's Tuesday evening fog alert warned that dawn mist and fog could bring visibility down to 200 metres in coastal, forest and mountainous areas, and advised drivers to use fog lights where necessary. Sunny weather with occasional cloud is forecast after the mist, followed by afternoon or evening thunderstorms or rain in parts of the south.

Accra is forecast to reach 33°C at noon, while Kumasi is expected to hit 34°C with a 40% chance of an evening storm. Across the south, Takoradi and Axim face a 30% chance of morning rain, reaching 31°C by afternoon, when thunderstorms are forecast.

gh.headline: Ghanaian actor takes coaching and acting roles on international thriller
gh.dek: Andrew Tandoh-Adote will coach performers and appear in The Neighbor, a Keyscott Entertainment production filming in South Africa and the US.
paragraphs: Ghanaian actor Andrew Tandoh-Adote has been appointed acting coach on The Neighbor, an upcoming thriller produced by US company Keyscott Entertainment. He will also act in the film, which is being shot in South Africa and the United States.

Tandoh-Adote said veteran Ghanaian playwright Uncle Ebo Whyte first spotted his ability to guide fellow actors during theatre rehearsals and later gave him coaching duties in some of his productions. Tandoh-Adote said he had not expected the skill to earn him income; his name now appears on a production chair as acting coach.
The film’s cast includes Ghanaian dancehall artiste Stonebwoy and actress Ama K. Abebrese, Nigerian actress Osas Ighodaro and American actor Myles Truitt.

cd.headline: Tshisekedi sets four demands for Congo to process more minerals at home
cd.dek: At a Kinshasa economic forum, the president said reliable energy, infrastructure, skills and a fight against misconduct are needed for the shift.
paragraphs: Democratic Republic of Congo President Félix Tshisekedi said on Monday, 23 November, that the country should move beyond producing minerals and build an economy able to process and manufacture more of them. He set out four requirements at the launch of the 12th Makutano Economic Forum in Kinshasa: more energy, durable infrastructure, investment in skills and a fight against misconduct.

Tshisekedi said reliable, competitively priced electricity was needed for domestic refining and mineral processing. He argued that factories should not face power shortages despite Congo's large electricity potential.

The forum was held alongside Makutano Mining 2026 under the theme “Mining sovereignty in action”. Tshisekedi said mineral sovereignty depended on turning underground resources into lasting economic wealth.
